name: Saint Cecilia
history: A Roman virgin and martyr whose name is said in the Roman Canon. The story of her martyrdom says she sang to God in her heart, and so she became the patron of music and musicians. Her body was found incorrupt in 1599.
meditation: Sing, or listen to, one piece of sacred music today with full attention.
life: Cecilia was venerated in Rome from early times, and her name stands in the Roman Canon of the Mass. The story of her life comes from her Acts, written long after her death and largely legendary. They tell that she was a Christian of noble family who had vowed her virginity to God and was married against her will to Valerian, a pagan. On their wedding night she told him of her vow and of the angel who guarded her; Valerian was baptised, and with his brother Tiburtius was martyred. Cecilia was then condemned, survived an attempt to suffocate her in the bath of her house, and died of wounds from the sword. The church of Santa Cecilia in Trastevere is said to stand on the site of her home. She became the patron of musicians because an antiphon speaks of music played at her wedding.
prayerTo: Saint Cecilia, virgin and martyr, you sang to the Lord in your heart while the music of the world played around you. Pray for musicians and all who lead the Church's song, and for me, that my whole life may become a hymn of praise, faithful to Christ in every trial. Amen.
penance: Sing a hymn today, alone or with others, or support your parish choir. Keep a quiet hour without background music, to listen to God.
prayer: O God, Who gladden us by the annual feast of blessed Cecilia, Your Virgin and Martyr, grant, we beseech You, that we may by virtuous conduct follow her whom we venerate in this sacred rite. Through our Lord Jesus Christ. Amen.
prayerSource: Collect of the day, Roman Missal of 1962
